universal_lens: The tactical state space is governed by a piecewise velocity vector field. gsi_mapping: GSI models the defensive line's backward displacement as a stochastic process. Bayesian updating occurs when the tackle blocks; the posterior distribution shifts the runner's optimal path toward the center. Conformal prediction intervals bound the success probability of the secondary gap exploitation based on historical blocking frequencies.

primitives.name: Right-Angle Tackle Deflection
primitives.verbatim_quote: This is taken advantage of by developing a style of play where the backs, after having started, run at medium speed parallel to the rush line and then drive by the tackle by making a rightangle turn when opposite him.
primitives.latex: \mathbf{v}(t) = \begin{cases} v_0 \hat{i}, & x(t) < x_T \\ v_0 \hat{j}, & x(t) \geq x_T \end{cases}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: v_0: scalar velocity (m/s), \hat{i}: unit vector parallel to line (dimensionless), \hat{j}: unit vector perpendicular to line (dimensionless), x(t): longitudinal position (m), x_T: tackle's transverse coordinate (m)
primitives.assumptions: Constant pre-turn velocity, instantaneous directional change upon reaching the transverse coordinate of the defensive tackle, frictionless kinematic plane.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity arises if the defensive tackle anticipates the derivative discontinuity, applying a counter-force that nullifies the orthogonal momentum transfer.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE boundary collision logic where an agent alters its heading vector by exactly \pi/2 upon intersecting a specific spatial threshold defined by an opposing agent.
layer2.telemetry: Measured via the angle of the runner's velocity vector immediately post-intersection relative to the line of scrimmage.

primitives.name: Central Axis Regression
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the tackle blocks the play, the runner noses back toward the center and tries to work through, where either the defensive guard or center has been carried back.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Delta \mathbf{r}_{reg}: regression displacement vector (m), k: proportional response coefficient (s^-1), \nabla \Phi_{block}: gradient of the blocking potential field (N/kg), \mathcal{D}_{gap}: stochastic diffusion through the vacated central gap (m^2/s)
primitives.assumptions: The blocking event creates a localized high-potential barrier, forcing the system to seek the lowest energy path back toward the origin (center).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the central gap is not vacated; the defensive guard/center remains stationary, causing the regression vector to collide with a solid boundary.

layer2.mapping: Represents a fallback policy in GSE reinforcement learning, triggered when the primary action space is occluded, redirecting the agent toward the highest probability vacuum in the defensive distribution.
layer2.telemetry: Yards gained following a blocked lateral play, correlated with the depth of the defensive center's backward displacement.

primitives.name: Offensive Spatial Translation
primitives.verbatim_quote: A good kick transfers the struggle one third the length of the field nearer the opponent's goal.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S_{new}: new starting coordinate along the pitch (m), S_{old}: previous coordinate (m), L: total length of the playing field (m)
primitives.assumptions: The field is a normalized 1D manifold [0, L]. The kick acts as a deterministic shift operator rather than a continuous differential movement.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under adverse environmental vectors (wind/drag) or defensive coverage functions that reduce the effective translation magnitude below the L/3 threshold.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a discrete jump process in GSI probabilistic modeling, instantly updating the prior distribution of scoring probability by advancing the state index by a fixed macroscopic step.
layer2.telemetry: Net yards gained per kick attempt, normalized against the total field length.

By running parallel to the rush line at a constant velocity $v_0$, the offensive back minimizes the time the defense has to adjust their lateral positioning. When the runner's longitudinal coordinate matches the tackle's ($x = x_T$), the velocity vector instantaneously rotates by $\pi/2$. This exploits the inertia of the defensive line, who are often 'carried back' (Quote 1), creating a temporal-spatial vacuum. However, this operator possesses a critical failure mode: if the tackle reads the derivative discontinuity and applies a blocking force, the orthogonal deflection fails. Here, the system invokes the 'central_regression_kernel' (Quote 3). The runner's control policy switches from lateral expansion to central contraction, seeking the lowest potential energy path back through the center, relying on the assumption that the defensive guard or center has been pulled away from the origin. Simultaneously, the text introduces the 'spatial_translation_kick' (Quote 6). Unlike the continuous differential equations governing the running plays, the kick is a discrete jump operator acting on the 1D spatial domain of the field. It forcibly shifts the state variable $S$ (line of scrimmage) by $L/3$. This duality—continuous local navigation versus discrete global translation—forms the core mathematical structure of the early football engine. The kicking formation itself (Quotes 8, 9) is a geometric optimization problem, arranging mass distributions to maximize the protective potential well around the kicker, ensuring the translation operator executes without interruption.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: These primitives trace back to the late 19th-century formalization of American football tactics, moving away from the chaotic mob-play era. The mathematical lineage connects to early kinematic theories of motion and basic vector calculus applied to physical contests. The concept of exploiting defensive momentum ('carried back') mirrors Newtonian principles of inertia, while the structured kicking game reflects the emerging application of geometric probability to sports strategy.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The offensive agents model the defensive line as reactive masses subject to inertial drag. The back assumes the tackle will commit laterally or be pulled backward by the initial parallel run. Conversely, the defensive agents are modeled as predictive filters attempting to anticipate the non-differentiable turn. The 'nosing back' maneuver explicitly accounts for the defender's successful prediction, requiring the runner to dynamically update their internal model of the defensive gaps and exploit the newly created central void.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A cross-layer veto is triggered if the discrete translation operator (the kick) is attempted without satisfying the geometric protection constraints of the formation. If the distribution of linemen does not form a sufficient potential barrier, the kick is vetoed in favor of a continuous ground operator. Furthermore, if the defensive center fails to regress (remains at the origin), the central_regression_kernel is vetoed, as the assumed vacuum does not exist, preventing the runner from safely reversing direction.
